qs.q: A man is evaluated for infertility and gynecomastia, revealing small firm testes, a 47,XXY karyotype, elevated gonadotropins, and low testosterone. What diagnosis do these findings support?
qs.e: Klinefelter syndrome is characterized by primary testicular failure due to a 47,XXY karyotype, leading to high gonadotropins, low testosterone, and small firm testes. Kallmann syndrome presents with low, rather than high, gonadotropins.
qs.s: Chemical Pathology — — Cardiovascular System Pathology: MCQs

qs.q: In a male infertility workup, what does an elevated serum FSH level combined with azoospermia typically indicate?
qs.e: Primary testicular failure destroys seminiferous tubules and reduces inhibin B feedback, causing FSH to rise significantly. Obstructive azoospermia typically presents with normal serum FSH levels.

qs.q: Swine fed on corn with a high moisture level of 22% stored at alternating temperatures between 7 and 21°C develop vulval swelling, prolapse, and infertility. What is the mechanism of action of the toxin causing these signs?
o: Binds to estrogen receptors as a weak estrogen
Targets the renal proximal tubule to cause disease
Inhibits protein and nucleic acid synthesis
Acts as a potent smooth muscle contractor
qs.e: Zearalenone functions as a weak estrogen by binding to estrogen receptors, causing reproductive issues like infertility, abortion, and vulval swelling, particularly in swine. Smooth muscle contraction and dopamine mimicry are features of ergot alkaloids.

qs.q: A tall, post-pubertal male is evaluated for infertility and gynecomastia. Cytogenetic testing reveals a 47,XXY karyotype. What is the expected underlying hormonal profile?
o: Normal levels of FSH, LH, and testosterone
qs.e: Primary testicular failure in Klinefelter syndrome causes hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, characterized by low testosterone and compensatory elevated FSH and LH. Low gonadotropin levels would indicate secondary hypogonadism.
qs.s: Genetics & Disease: Muscular Dystrophy, CF, Marfan, Diabetes, Cancer: MCQs

qs.q: A 32-year-old woman is evaluated for primary infertility. Hormonal and genetic testing reveals a 47,XXY karyotype. Which category of testicular infertility does this condition represent?
qs.e: Klinefelter syndrome is characterized by a 47,XXY karyotype and is a well-known genetic cause of primary testicular infertility and hypogonadism. It is distinct from mechanical causes like cryptorchidism or varicocele.

qs.q: A 30-year-old man is evaluated for infertility and a history of childhood mumps infection complicated by orchitis. Which microscopic change is most characteristic of the severe sequelae of mumps orchitis in adults?
o: Presence of intratubular germ cell neoplasia
Presence of tubular atrophy and fibrosis
qs.e: Mumps orchitis involves a lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate that can lead to severe necrosis, tubular atrophy, fibrosis, and subsequent sterility. Caseous granulomatous inflammation is characteristic of tuberculous epididymo-orchitis.
qs.s: Penile & Testicular Pathologies: Hypospadias, Tumors, Torsion – Male: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following uterine conditions is characterized by the presence of ectopic endometrial tissue outside the uterine cavity and frequently causes pelvic pain and infertility?
qs.e: Endometriosis is the presence of ectopic endometrial tissue located outside the uterus, leading to clinical manifestations like pain and infertility. Unlike adenomyosis, which stays within the myometrium, endometriosis implants in extrauterine sites.
qs.s: Female Reproductive Pathology: HPV, Cancer, PCOS & Pregnancy: MCQs

qs.q: A 30-year-old woman being evaluated for infertility undergoes diagnostic laparoscopy, which reveals red-brown nodules on the serosal surface of her pouch of Douglas and scarred, sealed fallopian tube fimbriae. Which of the following histologic criteria is required to definitively diagnose this condition?
o: Stromal decidualization and prominent vascular congestion
Basal endometrial layer invagination and myometrial hypertrophy
Koilocytocytic atypia and multinucleated giant cells
Endometrial glands, endometrial stroma, and hemosiderin pigment
qs.e: Definitive histologic diagnosis of endometriosis requires at least two of three features: endometrial glands, endometrial stroma, and hemosiderin pigment. Hypertrophy of the myometrium is characteristic of adenomyosis rather than endometriosis.

ai.subject: Obstetrics & gynaecology
ai.summary: Infertility is the failure to conceive after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse. In East Africa, infections, malnutrition and herbal remedies are common causes. A systematic history, basic exam and affordable tests guide management.

sections.p: Infertility is defined as the inability to achieve pregnancy after 12 months of regular, unprotected sex in a healthy couple. Diagnosis requires a 12‑month history, confirmation of ovulation, and assessment of the partner’s semen.
b: Unexplained infertility – no identifiable cause after work‑up
Primary infertility – never conceived; secondary – failed a previous pregnancy

t.b: Rule out thyroid, prolactin, diabetes – abnormal results suggest endocrine causes
Detect uterine fibroids, ovarian cysts, tubal patency (if available) – normal findings reduce surgical suspicion
Assess volume, concentration, motility, morphology – abnormality indicates male factor infertility

sections.p: Infertility is staged by cause and duration. The WHO classification of male factor infertility grades sperm concentration and motility. Tubal disease is staged by extent of blockage.
b: WHO Grade I – mild male factor; Grade III – severe

sections.p: In low‑resource settings, infections dominate. Other common causes include malnutrition, hormonal imbalance and traditional medicine.
b: Malnutrition – protein‑energy wasting affects ovarian reserve

sections.p: Patients report a long period of trying to conceive with no success. Women may have irregular periods, pain, or history of infections. Men may notice low libido or erectile dysfunction.
b: History of fever or genital ulcers

sections.p: Use the most affordable tests available. When a test is unavailable, rely on clinical clues and basic labs.
b: Urine pregnancy test – rule out pregnancy before investigations

sections.p: Urgent referral is needed for signs of severe infection, haemorrhage or ectopic pregnancy.
b: Severe genital ulceration – risk of HIV transmission

sections.p: Treat the underlying cause first, then offer assisted reproduction if needed. In low‑resource settings, focus on affordable, evidence‑based care.
b: Refer for IVF only if other options fail and resources allow

sections.p: Regular review every 3–6 months. Prevention focuses on STI control, malaria prophylaxis and safe sexual practices.
b: Counselling on family planning and safe sex

sections.p: Infertility can be mistaken for subfertility, early menopause or contraceptive failure.
b: Contraceptive failure – use of barrier methods with incorrect use

sections.p: Some tests may give false negatives or positives in low‑resource settings.
b: Rapid HIV test – window period may miss recent infection

faq.q: How do you differentiate primary from secondary infertility?
faq.a: Primary infertility is never having conceived; secondary is failure after a previous successful pregnancy.

faq.q: Which infection is most common cause of tubal infertility in East Africa?
faq.a: Chlamydia trachomatis, often asymptomatic, leading to tubal scarring.

exam: A 28‑year‑old woman with 18 months of infertility and a history of untreated PID presents. What is the next best investigation? — Pelvic ultrasound to assess tubal patency and ovarian reserve.
A 32‑year‑old man has azoospermia on semen analysis. What is the most likely cause in a low‑resource setting? — Undiagnosed HIV or untreated STIs causing testicular damage.
A patient with infertility is taking an herbal abortifacient. What is the most probable mechanism of infertility? — Antagonism of gonadotrophin‑releasing hormone leading to ovarian suppression.
A couple has unexplained infertility after normal work‑up. What is the first assisted reproduction option? — Intrauterine insemination if male factor is mild and facilities exist.
A woman with infertility has a normal FSH but irregular periods. What endocrine disorder should be ruled out? — Hypothyroidism.
A patient presents with infertility and severe anemia. What urgent condition must be excluded? — Ectopic pregnancy or severe infection.
A 25‑year‑old woman with infertility has a history of malaria. What is the likely impact on fertility? — Malaria‑related anemia and possible ovarian dysfunction.
A man with infertility is on a pesticide‑heavy farm. What is a potential cause? — Environmental toxin exposure causing sperm DNA damage.
